title: Centaurium erythraea subsp. methanol Rafn
author: Matekalo, Dragana
license_note: Zenodo record metadata license field: cc-zero

steps.title: Set up UHPLC‑MS/MS method
steps.instruction: Prepare the UHPLC‑MS/MS system using a mobile phase containing acetic acid (as described in Banjanac et al. 2017). Perform product‑ion‑scanning (PIS) experiments on methanol extracts of C. erythraea to obtain MS² spectra for the five target secoiridoids and record the following diagnostic fragment ions for each compound:

substeps.instruction: Loganin (1): [M+CH₃COOH‑H]⁻ m/z 449, Rt = 3.05 min; fragments m/z 227 (loss of glucose) and m/z 127 (1,4 F).
Secologanin (2): [M+CH₃COOH‑H]⁻ m/z 447, Rt = 3.72 min; fragments m/z 155 (RDA cleavage) and m/z 123 (loss of glucose + H₂O + CO + C₂O₂).
Sweroside (3): [M+CH₃COOH‑H]⁻ m/z 417, Rt = 3.05 min; fragments m/z 195 (loss of glucose) and m/z 179 (deprotonated glucose).
Swertiamarin (4): [M+CH₃COOH‑H]⁻ m/z 433, Rt = 3.59 min; fragments m/z 179 (deprotonated glucose) and m/z 161 (glucose‑H₂O).
Gentiopicrin (5): [M+CH₃COOH‑H]⁻ m/z 415, Rt = 2.59 min; fragments m/z 179 (deprotonated glucose) and m/z 119 (loss of glucose + H₂O + C₂O₂).
Using the two most intense fragments for each compound, program selected‑reaction‑monitoring (SRM) transitions for quantitative analysis.

steps.title: Run quantitative UHPLC‑MS/MS
steps.instruction: Inject the prepared C. erythraea methanol extracts and acquire SRM data according to the transitions defined above, recording peak areas, retention times and m/z values for loganin, secologanin, sweroside, swertiamarin and gentiopicrin.

steps.title: Confirm compounds by UHPLC‑DAD
steps.instruction: Perform a parallel UHPLC run equipped with a diode‑array detector (DAD). Compare the UV spectra and retention times (Rt) of each peak with those of authentic reference standards; use the λmax values listed in Table S1 for verification.

steps.title: Identify SG pathway genes via BLAST
steps.instruction: Access the transcriptome dataset of C. erythraea aerial parts. Conduct BLAST searches using the following Catharanthus roseus MIA pathway genes as queries: geranyl diphosphate synthase (GPPS), geraniol synthase (GES), geraniol‑8‑oxidase (G8O), 8‑hydroxygeraniol oxidoreductase (8HGO), iridoid synthase (IS), iridoid oxidase (IO), 7‑deoxyloganetic acid glucosyltransferase (7DLGT), 7‑deoxyloganic acid hydrolase candidates (7DLH1, 7DLH2), loganic acid O‑methyltransferase (LAMT) and secologanin synthase (SLS). Retrieve also two candidate cytochrome P450 reductase (CPR) genes. Select all hits showing >70 % sequence similarity to the query proteins.

steps.title: Design gene‑specific primers
steps.instruction: For each selected candidate gene (including the two CPRs), design primers suitable for quantitative PCR (qPCR) and regular PCR, ensuring specificity and optimal melting temperature.

steps.title: Amplify and verify candidate genes
steps.instruction: Perform regular PCR using the designed primers to amplify each candidate gene from C. erythraea cDNA. Run a real‑time PCR (qPCR) and analyse the dissociation curves to confirm single‑product amplification.

steps.title: Sequence PCR products
steps.instruction: Purify the PCR amplicons obtained with the qPCR primers and submit them for Sanger sequencing. Align the obtained sequences with the original transcriptome contigs to confirm gene identity.
